messages.content: I am planning for MS in Data Science in Germany for Fall 2026. My budget is around 15 lakhs.

Hi Pooja Reddy! Managing an MS in Data Science in Germany on a 15-lakh INR budget is entirely achievable, especially when targeting public universities. 

Here is the financial breakdown for your first year, keeping in mind the public university system and mandatory visa requirements:

| Expense Item | Original Currency | INR Equivalent (Approx.) |
|--------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| **Tuition Fees (Public)** | ~€300 / semester | ~₹54,000 / year |
| **Living Expenses (Blocked Account)** | €11,904 / year | ~₹10,80,000 / year |
| **Health Insurance & Misc. Fees** | €30,000 coverage (~€1,100/yr) | ~₹1,00,000 / year |
| **Visa & Transfer Fees** | ~€225 | ~₹21,000 |
| **Total Estimated First-Year Budget** | **~€13,500+** | **~₹12,55,000+** |

Target public universities in Germany for your MS in Data Science because they charge zero tuition fees, requiring only a semester contribution fee (roughly €300 per semester) which often includes your public transport ticket. Your 15-lakh budget comfortably covers the mandatory blocked account requirement (€11,904 per year as per current guidelines) and initial setup costs, leaving a buffer for travel and incidental expenses, Pooja Reddy.

Will my 15 lakhs cover the German blocked account and living costs?

Monthly withdrawals are capped at €992 to cover daily sustenance, leaving a safe buffer from that initial 15-lakh pool for flight tickets and initial setup costs.
